Subject: Novathera call — verification pack + immediate next steps

Thanks again for your time today — good discussion. Quick recap and concrete next steps so we keep momentum: 

Summary of call
- Goal: productionize customer-facing summarization and search assistant for clinical notes (throughput target: ~250 qps at 2s latency P95 for 512-token queries).
- Constraints: PHI-sensitive, must run in customer VPC, preference for quantized 4-bit variants if quality acceptable.
- Key risks flagged: hallucination on code/structured fields, regression vs. current baseline on clinical abbreviations.

Action items (I've assigned owners):
1) Redwood verification pack (what I'm attaching/ sharing): recommended model shortlist, TPS/latency percentile snapshots, prompt set we used for QA, and a one-page risk summary — OWNER: Redwood (Ben) — ETA: EOD Thu 3/15
2) Pilot proposal (VPC/private pilot + data handling checklist) — OWNER: Vivek — ETA: Mon 3/20
3) Your asks: provide a small sample set of redacted notes (50 documents) to run the prompt pack — OWNER: Novathera — ETA: Tue 3/21

What I'm sharing now (links/attachments):
- novathera_prompt_set_v1.jsonl — the prompt/ground-truth pairs I used for our run (short, focused on abbreviations and structured extractions)
- redwood-verif-20280314-summary.pdf — one-page at-a-glance: recommended models and the TPS/latency percentiles we observed 
- Drive folder with full traces and per-model logs: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cNovatheraPerfPack

I'll call out the recommended models below with the quick rationale so you have it in writing.

Recommended shortlist (first-pass):
- rw-micro-7b-q4f: best cost-performance; strong recall on long-context summaries in our prompts, P95 ~1.8s at 250 qps (with batching and local KV cache hit ~35%).
- rw-std-13b-8k: higher quality on edge cases/abbrev expansion but 2.6s P95 at same load; suggested for canary on critical flows.
- rw-reduced-13b-int8: middle ground for customers wanting lower latency without moving to 7b quality drop; good for extraction tasks.

Questions for you: can you confirm compliance contacts (SOC2 evidence path) and whether the sample redaction will include PHI markers? That affects how we prepare the pilot packaging.

Thanks — I'll follow up internally to link the perf dashboard and attach the short report.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen

Stephanie / Vivek — short perf summary and quick notes attached and below. I annotated the Drive traces (see link) — the one-pager PDF in the folder is now updated with quantization flags.

Quick table (observed, with Redwood runtime defaults and KV cache enabled where noted):
- rw-micro-7b-q4f: 250 qps -> P50 0.95s / P95 1.82s / P99 2.90s ; throughput at that config sustained ~265 TPS (KV cache hit ~34%). (quantized 4-bit run)
- rw-reduced-13b-int8: 250 qps -> P50 1.15s / P95 2.45s / P99 3.8s ; sustained TPS ~235 (INT8 run)
- rw-std-13b-8k: 250 qps -> P50 1.6s / P95 2.62s / P99 4.1s ; sustained TPS ~190 (FP16 run; recommended for canary critical flows)

Quality regressions flagged (from prompt_set_v1 runs):
- Abbreviation expansion: rw-micro-7b-q4f occasionally expands GFR incorrectly on lab values — (seen in 6/200 samples).
- ICD extraction: rw-reduced-13b-int8 missed structured ICD codes in 4/200 samples — suggest adding a focused eval and a small calibration prompt.
- Hallucination: rw-std-13b-8k had higher precision on rare clinical phrases, but still produced occasional invented medication routes; flag for guardrail prompt.

Attachments (in Drive folder and attached one-pager): redwood-verif-20280314-summary.pdf (updated), novathera_prompt_set_v1.jsonl, per-model-traces.tar.gz (trace stubs).

Next recommended customer-facing note to Evan:
- Offer the 7b q4f variant as cost-effective baseline for a 4-week pilot (we can set a canary route to route 10% to 13b-8k for critical docs).
- Include our KB on prompt guardrails and a suggested calibration prompt to reduce abbreviation errors (I attached a short example in the Drive).

I'll draft the short EOD note you can send to Evan if you want.

Ben Carter
